questions.q: In dense fog you can see only the rear lights of the car ahead. Why is it dangerous to follow them closely?
options: If it brakes hard, you will not be able to stop in time
On the contrary, following closely behind a car in fog is safer
It is dangerous only at night, in daytime fog is no problem
It is dangerous only for trucks with a long braking distance
questions.explain: In fog it is easy to become “glued” to the lights ahead: they create a false sense of security (UK Highway Code, para. 235), but you have no margin in either distance or time, and you learn about an obstacle only from the brake lights. Keep a longer following distance than usual and a speed at which you can stop within the distance you can see ⟦16⟧.

questions.q: On a highway you enter a stretch of dense fog. What is the correct way to act?
options: Keep your speed to get through the fog quickly and not hold anyone up
Reduce speed smoothly, switch on dipped headlights, increase your following distance
Brake hard and stop right in your lane with the hazard warning lights on
Switch on main-beam headlights to see further along the road and drive as before
questions.explain: Hard braking in fog often ends in a rear-end collision: the driver behind you also sees poorly. Reduce speed smoothly, checking your mirrors. In poor visibility, use dipped headlights, and front fog lamps may be used too ⟦17⟧, while main beam reflects off the fog and worsens visibility.

questions.q: In dense fog you can see the road for about 50 m. A tractor is moving slowly ahead. May you overtake it by moving into the oncoming lane?
options: Yes, if you switch on main-beam headlights and front fog lamps
Yes, if you sound the horn before overtaking
Yes, if the tractor is driving slower than 20 km/h and the overtaking will be short
No: you cannot make sure the oncoming lane is clear for overtaking
questions.explain: Before overtaking, the driver must make sure the oncoming lane is clear for a sufficient distance ahead ⟦18⟧. Overtaking on a highway needs hundreds of metres, and in fog you can see only 50 m, so you cannot make sure of this. Main beam in fog only dazzles, and the horn is no substitute for a clear view.

questions.q: You are driving from Astana to Almaty, about 1200 km. What is the safest way to plan the trip?
options: Set off at night after the working day so as not to lose time during the day
Drive without stopping, staying alert with coffee and energy drinks
Take a break every 2 hours and, if possible, split the journey over 2 days
Drive as fast as possible to spend less time at the wheel
questions.explain: Such a journey takes 12-15 hours at the wheel, and fatigue is unavoidable. A break of at least 15 minutes every 2 hours is recommended (UK Highway Code, para. 91), and an overnight stop on the way or a change of driver reduces the risk of falling asleep. Driving a vehicle while fatigued is prohibited ⟦19⟧, and coffee and energy drinks help only for a short time.

questions.q: You are driving alongside the rear of a truck, and it has switched on its right direction indicator. What is the best thing to do?
options: Sound your horn and stay alongside so as not to give up your place
Accelerate sharply and shoot ahead before it starts to move over
Slow down and let it go: it most likely cannot see you
Stay alongside: it must let you pass when changing lanes
questions.explain: Under the Rules, a driver changing lanes gives way to those travelling in the same direction without changing lanes ⟦20⟧. But alongside the rear of a truck you are in its blind spot, and the driver may not notice you. It is better not to argue but to give it room and not linger beside a large vehicle.

questions.q: You want to change into the left lane. The mirror shows nothing, but when you look over your shoulder you notice a motorcyclist. What should you do?
options: Change lanes: your indicator is already on
Change lanes: the motorcyclist will move away himself
Sound your horn and change lanes
Let the motorcyclist pass and change lanes after him
questions.explain: A motorcycle easily hides in the blind spot of the mirrors. When changing lanes, you give way to those travelling in the same direction without changing lanes ⟦21⟧, and a switched-on indicator gives you no priority ⟦22⟧.

questions.q: What is the best way to adjust the side mirrors to reduce the blind spot?
options: Mirror adjustment does not affect the blind spot
So that the edge of your own body takes up only a narrow strip in the mirror
So that mainly your own car is visible in the mirror
Point them at the asphalt by the rear wheels
questions.explain: The more of your own body is in the mirror, the less you see to the side. If your car takes up only a narrow strip at the edge, the adjacent lane is visible more widely. But even well-adjusted mirrors do not remove the blind spot completely, so look over your shoulder before a manoeuvre.

questions.q: Ahead, a cyclist is riding near the right edge, and there is a pothole in front of him. A car is approaching from the opposite direction. What should you do?
options: Slow down and overtake once the pothole and the oncoming car are behind you
Overtake at once, moving close to the cyclist, to make it in time
Sound your horn so the cyclist moves onto the shoulder, and overtake
Pass between the cyclist and the oncoming car without reducing speed
questions.explain: Before the pothole, the cyclist will almost certainly swerve left, right into your path. You may overtake when there is enough room for a safe lateral clearance ⟦23⟧ and the oncoming lane is clear ⟦24⟧. The horn is used only to warn of overtaking outside built-up areas or to prevent a crash ⟦25⟧.

questions.q: You want to turn right, and a cyclist is riding along the edge of the carriageway ahead. What should you do?
options: Overtake him and turn right immediately in front of him
Sound your horn so he stops and lets you through
Turn, crossing his path: a car has priority
Let him pass and turn after him
questions.explain: If you overtake a cyclist and turn right away, you will “cut him up”, and he will not have time to brake. It is calmer to let him go past and turn after him. Before turning right, take the far right position ⟦26⟧.

questions.q: You are approaching a school. There is a “Children” sign, and a group of children is on the pavement. What is the right way to drive through this section?
options: Drive through faster, before the children step onto the carriageway
Reduce speed, keep your foot near the brake, be ready to stop
Keep your speed: the children are on the pavement, not on the carriageway
Sound your horn so the children notice the car and move away from the road
questions.explain: Children may suddenly run into the road: after a ball, to a friend, without looking around. The “Children” sign warns of exactly this kind of section. Choose a speed at which you can stop if a hazard appears ⟦27⟧.

questions.q: A bus is standing at a stop on the right. What should you expect as you drive past it?
options: That the bus driver will always let you pass before pulling away
That the bus may start reversing towards your car
That a pedestrian may step out from behind the bus, so reduce speed
Nothing special: pedestrians must wait until the bus has left
questions.explain: Passengers who have got off a bus often cross the road in front of it or behind it, and the body of the bus hides them from view. Pass such a place slowly. In built-up areas, give way to a bus pulling away from a marked stop ⟦28⟧.

questions.q: Your light has just turned green. From the left, a blue car is approaching the intersection at high speed, although its light is already red. What should you do?
options: Do not move off until the blue car has passed or stopped
Go at once: you have a green light, and it must stop
Sound your horn so the blue car brakes, and go
Pull away sharply to get across the intersection before it
questions.explain: A green signal permits you to proceed, but it does not protect you from a driver who cannot or will not stop in time. On noticing a hazard, the driver reduces speed, even to the point of stopping ⟦29⟧. Waiting a couple of seconds is easier than taking a side impact.

questions.q: You are stopping in a traffic jam behind another car. How far back is it best to stop?
options: The distance in a jam does not matter, the main thing is not to fall behind
So that you can see the rear wheels of the car ahead
Right up close, almost touching the bumper, so nobody squeezes in
No less than 20 metres, as on a highway
questions.explain: If you can see the rear wheels of the car in front, there are a few metres between you. That is enough to drive around it if it stalls, and to avoid hitting it if you are struck from behind.

questions.q: Where do experienced drivers advise looking in traffic?
options: Only at the bumper of the car ahead, to brake in time
Mainly in the interior mirror, to see who is behind
More often at the speedometer, so as not to exceed the speed limit
Far ahead, 10-15 seconds along your route, and regularly in the mirrors
questions.explain: If you look only at the bumper ahead, you learn about braking last. Looking far ahead shows danger in advance: brake lights several cars ahead, a pedestrian at the edge, a car pulling out. The mirrors tell you whether there is somewhere to go.

questions.q: A hurrying driver behind you is flashing his headlights and sounding his horn. What should you do?
options: Speed up and do not let him past: let him wait
Gesture that he is in the wrong and drive on as before
When it is safe, change lanes and let him pass
Brake hard to teach him a lesson and make him back off
questions.explain: An argument on the road achieves nothing. Do not impede other drivers ⟦30⟧: if you are driving in the left lane slower than the permitted speed, clear it by moving right ⟦31⟧. Braking hard without necessity is also prohibited ⟦32⟧.

questions.q: At 90 km/h your front tyre bursts, and the car pulls to one side. What should you do?
options: Turn the steering wheel sharply the other way to straighten the car
Switch off the ignition at once and brake with the handbrake
Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, slow gradually
Brake hard until you stop completely, right in your lane
questions.explain: Hard braking or a sharp steering input on a flat tyre easily throws the car into a skid. Hold the steering wheel with both hands, ease off the accelerator and brake gently once your speed has dropped. After stopping, switch on the hazard warning lights if necessary and put out a warning triangle ⟦33⟧.

questions.q: The brake pedal suddenly goes to the floor, and the car is not braking. What should you do?
options: Stop the engine and take out the key so the wheels lock and the car stops at once
Sharply engage reverse gear while moving so the gearbox stops the car
Open the door, switch off the lights and get ready to jump out of the moving car
Pump the pedal, shift to a lower gear, apply the handbrake gradually
questions.explain: Rapid presses sometimes restore pressure in the system. A lower gear brakes with the engine, and the handbrake is applied gradually so as not to lock the wheels. You must not stop the engine: the power steering and brake assistance would stop working. Driving on with a defective service braking system is prohibited ⟦34⟧.

questions.q: You notice a cut in the sidewall of a tyre, with the cord visible in it. May you drive on?
options: Yes, if it is a rear wheel and you drive carefully
No: use is prohibited with the cord exposed
Yes, if the pressure in this tyre is normal and not falling
Yes, but no faster than 90 km/h and only as far as home
questions.explain: Local damage to a tyre (punctures, cuts, tears) that exposes the cord is a defect with which use of the vehicle is prohibited ⟦35⟧. Such a tyre may burst while driving, so fit the spare wheel.

questions.q: One wheel nut is missing from a wheel. May you drive like this?
options: No: driving without a wheel bolt or nut is prohibited
Yes, if the remaining nuts are tightened well
Yes, if the nut is missing from a rear wheel rather than a front one
Yes, but only in town and no faster than 60 km/h
questions.explain: A missing wheel bolt or nut is a defect under the List of Defects ⟦36⟧. The load on the remaining fixings increases, and the wheel may come off while driving.

questions.q: You are descending a long mountain serpentine road. What is the right way to brake?
options: Coast down in neutral, keeping a light pressure on the brake pedal all the time
Keep the brake pedal pressed all the way to the bottom
Switch off the engine and coast to save fuel
Use a lower gear so the engine brakes, and only brake lightly with the pedal
questions.explain: If you brake with the pedal alone the whole time, the brakes overheat and begin to hold worse. A lower gear brakes with the engine, and the pedal is used only for light braking. In neutral the car picks up more speed, and with the engine off the power assistance stops working.

questions.q: Ahead is a “Cattle crossing” sign, and beyond it a herd is grazing by the road. What should you do?
options: Move into the oncoming lane, away from the herd, and keep your speed
Reduce speed and be ready to stop: the cattle may come onto the road
Sound your horn in advance so the animals move away from the road
Drive through the section as fast as possible before the herd comes out
questions.explain: Animals are unpredictable: if one starts across the road, the others will follow. A loud horn may frighten them, and they may rush under your wheels. The horn is used only to warn of overtaking outside built-up areas or to prevent a crash ⟦37⟧. Pass slowly and with a wide margin ⟦38⟧.

questions.q: On an open steppe highway there is a “Crosswind” sign, and the wind is gusty. A truck is approaching from the opposite direction. What should you be ready for?
options: Having to switch on main-beam headlights because of dust
The engine possibly stalling from the wind
A sideways jerk: grip the steering wheel firmly and reduce speed
Nothing: strong wind affects only trucks
questions.explain: A gust of wind can shift the car noticeably sideways, and when passing an oncoming truck, the airflow first shields you from the wind and then hits again. Hold the steering wheel with both hands, reduce speed and increase the lateral clearance ⟦39⟧.
